chunks: Ibn Maḥbūb narrated from Ibrāhīm al-Karkhī, who said:
I said to Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام: What do you say about a man who bought from another man the wool of one hundred sheep, along with what is in their wombs of الحمل, for such-and-such dirhams?
So he عليه السلام said: There is no harm in that. If there is no pregnancy in their wombs, then his capital is in the wool.

key_terms.أَصْوَافَ: wool being sold in the transaction
key_terms.حَمْلٍ: pregnancy or fetus in the womb
key_terms.دِرْهَمًا: the payment amount in silver currency
key_terms.رَأْسُ مَالِهِ: his principal capital or underlying value
key_terms.لَا بَأْسَ: there is no legal problem or prohibition
key_terms.ٱلصُّوفِ: the wool that secures the sale's value

ai.seo_question: Is it permissible in Shia fiqh to buy wool together with what may be in the wombs of livestock?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling on purchasing wool together with the expected offspring in the wombs of sheep. The Imam عليه السلام permits the transaction, explaining that if no pregnancy exists, the buyer's principal value remains secured in the wool itself.

en.bab-ul-qaim-publications: Hadith.3853 - Ibn Mahbub narrated from Ibrahim Al-Karkhi who said:
I said to Abu Abdillah (as), "What do you say about a man who buys the wool of one hundred sheep and what is in their wombs in terms of pregnancy for such-and-such amount of dirhams?"
Imam (as) said: "There is no harm in that. If there is no pregnancy in their wombs, then his capital is in the wool."
